verifications.claim: The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older, ideally by the end of October.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "CDC recommends annual flu vaccination for everyone ages 6 months and older." (R2); "CDC recommends that people get a flu vaccine by the end of October." (R3); "Everyone 6 months and older should get a flu vaccine every season, ideally by the end of October" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state CDC's recommendation for everyone 6 months and older annually, with ideal timing by end of October.

verifications.claim: Standard-dose Shots are available for people 6 months and older.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Standard-dose flu vaccines without adjuvant... approved for individuals age 6 months and older" (R6); "Most inactivated flu vaccines are approved for people 6 months and older" (R10); "Standard-dose influenza shots... approved for use in children as young as 6 months" (R12)
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly confirm standard-dose shots approved for 6 months and older.

verifications.claim: High-dose & Adjuvanted Shots are specifically for adults 65 and older to create a stronger immune response.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Fluzone High-Dose Quadrivalent, a quadrivalent vaccine that contains four times the antigen of standard-dose" (R2); "Quadrivalent high-dose inactivated flu vaccine; Quadrivalent adjuvanted inactivated flu vaccine... for adults age 65 years and older" (R6); "High-dose... contains four times the amount of antigen... Adjuvanted flu vaccine (Fluad)... approved for people 65 years and older" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm high-dose and adjuvanted vaccines approved/recommended preferentially for 65+ with higher antigen/adjuvant for stronger response.

verifications.claim: Recombinant & Cell-based Shots are completely egg-free options.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Cell-based standard-dose flu vaccine... grown in cell culture"; "Recombinant flu vaccine (made without influenza viruses or eggs)" (R6); "A cell-based influenza shot (Flucelvax)... completely egg-free. A recombinant influenza shot (Flublok) which is a completely egg-free" (R12)
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state both recombinant and cell-based vaccines are egg-free.

verifications.claim: Nasal Spray (FluMist) is a live attenuated vaccine approved for healthy, non-pregnant individuals aged 2 through 49.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "FluMist Quadrivalent, an LAIV nasal spray vaccine, for use in people 2 to 49 years old" (R2); "Live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV4), a nasal-spray vaccine... approved for use in individuals age 2 years through 49 years. This vaccine is not recommended for use in pregnant women" (R6); "given to men and non-pregnant women 2 through 49 years of age" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct matches for FluMist as LAIV nasal spray approved 2-49 years, not for pregnant, and generally for healthy (not immunocompromised).

verifications.claim: It takes about two weeks for protection to develop after vaccination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Flu vaccines cause antibodies to develop in the body about two weeks after vaccination" (R2, R3); "It takes about 2 weeks for protection to develop after vaccination" (R7); "It takes about two weeks after vaccination for antibodies to develop" (R8, R12)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent direct statement across multiple references.

verifications.claim: Flu vaccines are available at doctors' offices, clinics, pharmacies, and health departments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Flu vaccines are offered at a wide range of locations, including doctors’ offices, health clinics, health departments, and pharmacies" (R5); "You can safely get a flu vaccine at multiple locations including your doctor’s office, health departments, and pharmacies" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing in R5 matches all locations listed.

verifications.claim: Flu vaccines are safe and cannot cause the flu.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "flu vaccines have an excellent safety profile"; "Injectable flu vaccines do not contain live flu viruses. Nasal spray... do not cause the flu" (R2); "The flu vaccine is safe for most people"; "No, a flu vaccine cannot cause flu illness" (R3); "A flu vaccine cannot cause flu" (R12)
verifications.reasoning: References affirm safety and explicitly state vaccines cannot cause flu.

verifications.claim: Children 6 months through 8 years may require two doses in one season.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Children 6 months through 8 years of age may need 2 doses during a single flu season" (R4, R7); "Some children need two doses of influenza vaccine" (R8, R12)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation for age group 6 months-8 years needing two doses.

verifications.claim: For the 2023-2024 season, all flu vaccines in the U.S. are designed to protect against four strains of the virus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "All flu vaccines available in the US for the 2023-2024 season are quadrivalent vaccines, which are designed to protect against 4 different flu viruses—2 influenza A viruses and 2 influenza B viruses" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 specifically for 2023-2024 season states all are quadrivalent (four strains).
